architecture.approach: Add crates/wirekit as a workspace member delivering M1 in dependency order. First the core contract (BP-005): a single #[non_exhaustive] WirekitError with stable W#### codes; one retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter, 3 attempts by default, retry on 5xx/429/network, honor Retry-After, never retry other 4xx); a hand-rolled per-provider token bucket; one shared reqwest::Client with HTTPS-only base URLs and a caller injection path; one auth layer (Bearer, Basic, API key header/query, HMAC, OAuth2 client credentials) over a redacting Secret<T>; tracing events for start, finish, retry, rate-limit hit, and error; and one request pipeline (auth, rate limit, retry, send, decode) with the CON-213 body-level error hook. Then four feature-gated provider modules built only against that contract: noaa, twilio, sendgrid, slack; each verifies webhooks over raw bytes (CON-215) and introduces no second error type. Then release preparation (BP-010): changelog, complete metadata, README with provider matrix, feature-flag table and error reference, one runnable example per provider, a verified cargo package --list and cargo publish -p wirekit --dry-run, and a wirekit section in RELEASING.md. The real publish and the wirekit-v0.1.0 tag stay manual post-merge. The core is always compiled; default = [] means no provider enabled. No application domain types, database, or global singleton.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/noaa.rs

components.description: The sendgrid feature module: bearer authentication, typed email, template, attachment, and contact models, sandbox mode, errors[] mapping with the full list retained, and ECDSA event-webhook verification on raw bytes.

dataModel.flowDescription: A provider builds a RequestSpec and hands it to its provider client, which delegates to the shared WirekitClient. The pipeline applies the configured auth scheme, acquires a token from the provider's bucket, sends the request through the shared reqwest::Client inside a retry loop, then decodes the body with serde and the optional body-level error hook. Every step maps failures into WirekitError. Provider-specific work is limited to request shaping (NOAA query parameters, Twilio form encoding, SendGrid JSON, Slack JSON), response decoding, canonical-form signing, and webhook signature verification over raw bytes. All state (client, buckets, OAuth2 token, NOAA cache, Slack channel cache) is in-process and dropped with the client; nothing is persisted or transmitted by the crate itself.

securityConsiderations.description: CON-511 Authentication: the pipeline applies the configured scheme to every outbound request for every provider (NOAA is intentionally auth-free and applies none) and fails closed with WirekitError::InvalidConfig when credentials are missing; secrets are wrapped in Secret<T>.
CON-514 Rate limiting: a per-provider/account token bucket is enforced before every outbound request, with per-provider overrides, so the aggregate rate per provider is respected.
CON-515 Input validation: URLs, header values, form bodies, and response bodies are validated; malformed input returns a typed WirekitError and never panics.
CON-519 Environment security: credentials come from caller-supplied configuration or secret stores; the crate never reads .env files and never commits a secret.
CON-520 HTTPS: non-HTTPS base URLs are rejected before any socket is opened, and all outbound requests use TLS; HSTS is documented as a deployment-edge concern.
CON-214 Secret redaction: secrets never appear in Debug, Display, logs, traces, or error payloads, and no secret field implements Serialize.
CON-215 Webhook verification: every provider verifier (Twilio HMAC-SHA1, SendGrid ECDSA, Slack HMAC-SHA256) operates on the raw request bytes and never re-serializes the body.
Provider secrets (auth tokens, API keys, signing secrets) are redacted in Debug, Display, logs, and traces across all four provider clients.
No committed credentials: documentation, examples, and fixtures contain placeholders only, and examples exit clearly when credentials are absent.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Token acquisition and retry backoff await an async timer; std::thread::sleep and busy-waiting are forbidden, so no runtime thread is blocked.
One shared reqwest::Client per process reuses TCP connections and applies default request timeouts and connection-pool limits.

Per-request work stays small: one bucket lookup, one header mutation set, and one decode; no per-request client or pool allocation. The NOAA module additionally caches forecasts and alerts by grid or zone with a configurable TTL, and Slack caches channel and user lookups, so repeated reads avoid the network entirely.

risks.description: A single crate carrying 26+ provider features becomes a release and build-time bottleneck.
risks.mitigation: M1 ships four providers; measure build times and propose a companion crate if needed (CON-104 amendment path).

risks.description: 0.x churn in the error, retry, or auth contract breaks provider modules.
risks.mitigation: #[non_exhaustive], stable W#### codes, an additive-only feature policy, and shared-pipeline use until the 1.0 freeze.

risks.description: A dependency raises its MSRV above 1.85.
risks.mitigation: The MSRV CI job fails fast; pin or downgrade with a recorded decision.

risks.description: rustls versus native-tls surprises on a platform.
risks.mitigation: rustls is the default and a documented feature selects native-tls.

risks.description: A secret leaks into logs, traces, an error payload, a fixture, or an example.
risks.mitigation: Secret<T>, no Serialize for secret fields, redacted tracing fields, placeholder-only fixtures, and property tests from the Test agent.

risks.description: A provider needs behavior the pipeline cannot express.
risks.mitigation: The body-level error hook, per-provider retry and rate-limit overrides, injectable clients, and canonical-form signing hooks.

risks.description: The rate limiter blocks the async runtime or is unfair under concurrency.
risks.mitigation: Async token acquisition, per-provider buckets, and EC-015.

risks.description: Twilio A2P 10DLC or toll-free verification is a launch blocker for SMS at scale.
risks.mitigation: The module is sender-agnostic; registration stays a consumer concern and is recorded as an open question, not a stub.

risks.description: SendGrid sender authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) or data residency limits real use.
risks.mitigation: The module is documented as transport-only; deliverability configuration stays with the consumer.

risks.description: Slack app review or scopes delay real use.
risks.mitigation: The module ships bot-token usage and documented scopes; the install flow is deferred to BP-015.

risks.description: NOAA polling across many workspaces is expensive in aggregate.
risks.mitigation: The optional grid/zone cache and a documented 15-minute polling budget.

risks.description: Provider error-shape drift (new codes, changed bodies) silently changes behavior.
risks.mitigation: Fixtures pin the shapes, unknown bodies map to WirekitError::Api rather than panicking, and tests are owned by /sdrive:test.

risks.description: Examples that need credentials cannot be verified in CI.
risks.mitigation: Examples compile in CI and exit with a clear message when credentials are absent; the NOAA example runs without a key.

risks.description: Scope creeps into other providers or stateful crates.
risks.mitigation: The explicit out-of-scope list; later work becomes a new version of this feature (CON-612).
